data.cultural_impact: The name Maran holds great significance in Hindu culture as it represents the god of death. It is a reminder of the cyclical nature of life and the inevitability of death. Maran is depicted in various art forms, mythological stories, and religious rituals.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, Maran represents the end of one life cycle and the beginning of another. He is a reminder of the impermanence of life and the importance of living in the present moment. Maran is also a symbol of detachment and letting go, as the soul leaves the physical body and transcends into the next world.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Maran was a general in the army of King Krishna during the Mahabharata war. The name Maran carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Maran was a loyal and brave warrior who fought on the side of the Pandava army against the Kauravas.
